findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.description:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns `nil` when no row exists, and line 107 calls `tu.notification_level` on it without a guard, giving a 500.

This is a reachable case rather than a theoretical one. The emailed link can be opened under a different logged-in account, or by a user whose row was never created.

Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)`, which already upserts (`app/models/topic_user.rb:77-118`), or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is exposed as an unauthenticated-intent GET
findings.description: Both unsubscribe routes are `get`, and the action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` using only the session cookie. No CSRF token or signed per-user key is involved, unlike the digest flow's `email/unsubscribe/:key`. - **Cross-site trigger:** any page or post that makes a logged-in browser fetch `/t///unsubscribe` (for example an `` tag) changes that user's notification level. The mutation at `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-113` runs before any format handling. - **Not idempotent:** the first request takes watching/tracking down to regular, and a second request takes regular down to muted. A refresh, mail-scanner prefetch or browser preload therefore silently escalates to muted. Render a confirmation page on GET and mutate on POST/PUT, or use a signed key and make the operation idempotent.

findings.title: Explicit `render :show` runs before `canonical_url` is set, dropping the canonical link on topic pages
findings.description:
`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block, so the view renders immediately. In `show`, `canonical_url ...` is only called afterwards, at `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:87`.

Before this change the HTML render was implicit and happened after the action finished, so `@canonical_url` was already set. Now `canonical_link_tag` (`lib/canonical_url.rb:14-16`, used in `app/views/layouts/_head.html.erb:9`) sees a nil `@canonical_url` and emits nothing. That is an SEO regression on every HTML topic page.

Move the `canonical_url` call above `perform_show_response`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so the change can be silently undone by auto-tracking
findings.description:
The action sets `notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. `TopicUser.change` (`app/models/topic_user.rb:87-90, 112-114`) additionally sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id = user_changed`, and publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event. None of that happens here.

The missing reason id matters. `update_last_read` (`app/models/topic_user.rb:160-167`) re-promotes a row to tracking whenever `notifications_reason_id is null` and the read-time threshold is exceeded. A user who was auto-tracked and then unsubscribes is flipped back to tracking the next time they read the topic.

The existing `set_notifications` action at `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:330-334` already uses `TopicUser.change`; this action should too.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every `add_unsubscribe_link` caller
findings.description:
The `unsubscribe_link` string in `config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` passes `template_args` straight to `I18n.t` at lines 67 and 90, with no default or presence check.

Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` now hits a missing-interpolation error. The existing spec had to be patched to add the argument (`spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172`), which is consistent with that.

The only in-tree caller, `app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:294-295`, supplies it. But the builder is a shared public entry point via `Email::BuildEmailHelper`, also used by plugins. Either make the topic-specific sentence conditional on `unsubscribe_url` being present, or validate it.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action, model method, or email link
findings.description:
The only test change adds an argument to an existing spec to keep it passing. I found no coverage for the following:

- **Controller action:** `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` has no `unsubscribe` reference, so the level transitions, slug redirect, login requirement and missing-`TopicUser` case are all untested.
- **Model method:** `Topic#unsubscribe_url` (`app/models/topic.rb:719-721`) has no spec.
- **Email content:** nothing asserts that the notification email actually contains the topic unsubscribe URL.
- **Client side:** nothing under `test/` references the new Ember route, controller or template.

A basic controller spec would have caught the nil crash above.

findings.title: Slug-mismatch redirect drops the request format and uses a permanent 301
findings.description:
The redirect goes to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`, which is an absolute URL with no format suffix (`app/models/topic.rb:719-721`). `redirect_to_correct_topic` (`app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:451-460`) preserves `.json`; this path does not, so a JSON request with a stale slug is redirected to the HTML endpoint.

A cacheable 301 onto a state-changing GET also compounds the idempotency problem in the second finding.

findings.title: Property name typo `stopNotificiationsText`
findings.description: "Notificiations" is misspelled. The template uses the same spelling (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3`), so it works, but it should be `stopNotificationsText`. The same file also has a stray trailing comma on line 7 and no terminating semicolon on line 9, unlike the neighbouring modules.

findings.title: Triple-stash rendering relies on server-side escaping of the title
findings.description: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML that includes `model.fancyTitle`. This is safe today only because `Topic#fancy_title` HTML-escapes the title server-side (`app/models/topic.rb:263-264`) and the translation string is trusted. No defect now; the escaping is not enforced at this boundary.

findings.title: Route overrides a computed property on a shared, identity-mapped details record
findings.description:
`topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` writes over a computed property defined in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/topic-details.js.es6:43-58`. The topic comes from `store.createRecord("topic", { id })`, which is identity-mapped (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:113-116, 204-227`), so the mutation is not local to this page.

I did not confirm how Ember 1.11.3 treats a set on this getter-style property. If it clobbers, the reason text may stay blank on the real topic page later in the same session. A display flag on the component would hide the text without touching model state.

findings.title: `List-Unsubscribe` header still points at user preferences
findings.description: The body now carries a per-topic unsubscribe link, but the `List-Unsubscribe` header still advertises only `user_preferences_url`. The same block has a redundant inner `if @opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` on line 107, which predates this change.

findings.title: Non-standard indentation in the reformatted `tracking` scope
findings.description: The chained `.where` is now indented three spaces and its arguments five. That matches neither the previous alignment nor the two-space convention used elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: Dropdown title guard
findings.description: Rendering the `<h4 class='title'>` only when `title` is set stops the literal "undefined" heading appearing where no title is passed, as in the new unsubscribe template. Existing callers that pass a title are unaffected.

findings.title: Client-side route, controller, view and template resolve correctly
findings.description: `topicUnsubscribe` resolves to `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` through the custom resolver's decamelize-and-slash lookup (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/ember/resolver.js.es6:148-161`), and the dasherized route, controller and view modules are found by `customResolve`. The static `/unsubscribe` segment does not clash with `topic.fromParamsNear`. This was checked by reading the resolver, not by running the app.

findings.title: Server route ordering and constraint cleanup
findings.description: The new routes sit ahead of the generic `t/:slug/:topic_id` routes and are constrained to a numeric `topic_id`. Removing the `post_number` constraint from the `summary` routes is harmless, since those paths have no `:post_number` segment.
